key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs and provides a conditional error analysis for the indirect approach.
engineering_relevance: This offers a principled way to train PINNs for PDE-constrained control problems while quantifying when residual-based predictions can be trusted.
method: Direct PINN: separate networks for state and control, optimized on a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: jointly learn state, adjoint, and control by enforcing the first-order optimality system.
Derive a conditional error decomposition and a computable residual indicator that accounts for approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft-constraint errors.
evidence_signal: The methods are evaluated on two manufactured test problems: a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear problem with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint.
watch_item: The reliability guarantees are conditional on regularity, neighborhood assumptions, and soft boundary/terminal constraints being sufficiently controlled, so implementation quality can strongly affect validity.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
